questions.question: In which state did Bharatanatyam originate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamil Nadu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bharatanatyam** is one of the oldest classical dance forms of India, tracing its origins back nearly **2,000 years** to the state of **Tamil Nadu**.
 
• The dance form is deeply rooted in the **Natya Shastra**, a comprehensive ancient Sanskrit text on the performing arts attributed to the sage **Bharata Muni**.
 
• Historically, it was performed as a solo dance by **Devadasis** (temple dancers) and was originally known as **Sadir Attam** or **Dasi Attam** in the royal courts and temples of South India.
 
• The name **Bharatanatyam** is a mnemonic, where **Bha** stands for **Bhava** (expression), **Ra** for **Raga** (melody), **Ta** for **Tala** (rhythm), and **Natyam** for dance.
 
• It is characterized by its fixed upper torso, bent legs, and knees flexed (**Aramandi** position), combined with spectacular footwork and a sophisticated vocabulary of sign language based on **Mudras** (hand gestures).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Karnataka**:

 
 
• This state is famous for the traditional theatre form known as **Yakshagana**, which combines dance, music, costume, and extemporaneous dialogue.
 
 
 
• **Gujarat**:
 
 
• Renowned for folk dances like **Garba** and **Dandiya Raas**, which are performed with great fervor during the **Navratri** festival.
 
 
 
• **Maharashtra**:
 
 
• Known for **Lavani**, a combination of traditional song and dance performed to the rhythmic beats of the **Dholki**.
 
 
 
• Famous Proponents:
 
 
• The revival of **Bharatanatyam** in the **20th century** was spearheaded by legendary figures such as **Rukmini Devi Arundale**, who founded **Kalakshetra**, and **E. Krishna Iyer**.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the Governor of Haryana in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ashim Kumar Ghosh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **February 2025**, the **President of India**, **Droupadi Murmu**, officially appointed **Ashim Kumar Ghosh** as the **Governor of Haryana**.
 
• He succeeds **Bandaru Dattatreya**, who had served as the **18th Governor** of the state since his appointment in **July 2021**.
 
• The **Governor** serves as the **Constitutional Head** of the state, and all **executive actions** of the **Government of Haryana** are formally carried out in his name.
 
• This appointment was made under **Article 155** of the **Constitution of India**, which states that the Governor shall be appointed by the **President** by warrant under his hand and seal.
 
• As the **nominal executive**, the Governor performs duties such as **summoning** the state legislature, **appointing** the **Chief Minister**, and giving **assent** to state bills.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constitutional Framework**:

 
 
• **Article 153**: Mandates that there shall be a **Governor** for each state in India.
 
• **Article 156**: Specifies that the Governor holds office during the **pleasure of the President**, usually for a term of **five years**.
 
• **Article 161**: Grants the Governor the power to **pardon** or **commute** sentences of any person convicted of any offense against state law.
 
 
 
• **Other Personalities**:
 
 
• **Kavinder Gupta**: A veteran politician who previously served as the **Deputy Chief Minister** of **Jammu and Kashmir**.
 
• **Manoj Kumar Singh**: A high-ranking **IAS officer** of the **1988 batch**, notably serving as the **Chief Secretary** of **Uttar Pradesh**.
 
• **Pusapati Ashok Gajapathi Raju**: A senior leader from **Andhra Pradesh** who served as the **Union Minister of Civil Aviation**.
 
 
 
• **Haryana State Overview**:
 
 
• **Formation**: The state was established on **November 1, 1966**, following the **Punjab Reorganisation Act**.
 
• **Capital**: **Chandigarh**, which is a **Union Territory** serving as the shared capital for **Haryana** and **Punjab**.
 
• **Raj Bhavan**: The official residence of the **Governor of Haryana** is located in **Chandigarh**.

questions.question: Which Indian bureaucrat was appointed Research and Analysis Wing (RAW) chief in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parag Jain**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Parag Jain**, a senior officer of the **Indian Police Service (IPS)** from the **1989 batch**, was appointed as the chief of the **Research and Analysis Wing (RAW)** in **January 2025**.
 
• He belongs to the **Himachal Pradesh cadre** and possesses extensive experience in national security and intelligence, having served significant tenures within the **Intelligence Bureau (IB)** and **RAW** itself.
 
• The **Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC)** cleared his name to lead the external intelligence agency for a fixed tenure, following the standard protocol for top security appointments in India.
 
• He took over the prestigious position from **Ravi Sinha**, whose tenure concluded in early **2025** after serving since June 2023.
 
• As the head of **RAW**, Jain is responsible for overseeing foreign intelligence, counter-terrorism operations, and providing strategic inputs to the **Prime Minister** and the **National Security Council**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Research and Analysis Wing (RAW)**:

 
 
• Founded: It was established on **September 21, 1968**, under the guidance of its first director, **R.N. Kao**, following intelligence gaps identified during the 1962 and 1965 wars.
 
• Structure: It functions under the **Cabinet Secretariat** and reports directly to the **Prime Minister of India**.
 
• Headquarters: Located in **New Delhi**.
 
 
 
• **Ravi Sinha**:
 
 
• A **1988-batch IPS officer** of the **Chhattisgarh cadre** who preceded Parag Jain as the **Secretary (Research)**.
 
 
 
• **Praveen Sood**:
 
 
• A **1986-batch IPS officer** who was appointed as the **Director** of the **Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)** in May 2023 for a two-year term.
 
 
 
• **Intelligence Bureau (IB)**:
 
 
• Unlike RAW, which handles external intelligence, the **IB** is India's **internal intelligence** agency and falls under the **Ministry of Home Affairs**.

questions.question: Water in the air is measured as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Humidity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Humidity** is defined as the concentration of **water vapor** present in the air. Water vapor is the gaseous state of water and is invisible to the human eye.
 
• The amount of water vapor in the atmosphere is primarily increased through **evaporation** from water bodies like oceans and lakes, and **transpiration** from plants.
 
• It is measured using a scientific instrument known as a **Hygrometer**. A specific type called a **Sling Psychrometer** uses two thermometers (dry bulb and wet bulb) to determine humidity levels.
 
• The capacity of air to hold moisture is directly related to its **temperature**; warmer air can hold more water vapor than colder air. When air reaches its maximum capacity, it is said to be **saturated**.
 
• **Relative Humidity** is the most common measurement used in **meteorology**, expressed as a percentage (%) of the amount of moisture the air holds relative to what it can hold at that temperature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Density**:

 
 
• In an atmospheric context, it refers to the **mass of air** per unit volume. It decreases with increasing **altitude** as the air molecules become more spread out.
 
 
 
• **Temperature**:
 
 
• This is the measure of the **average kinetic energy** of the particles in the air. It is measured using a **Thermometer** in units such as **Celsius**, **Fahrenheit**, or **Kelvin**.
 
 
 
• **Pressure**:
 
 
• **Atmospheric pressure** is the force exerted by the weight of the air column above a specific point. It is measured using a **Barometer**, typically in **millibars** (mb) or **Pascals** (Pa).

questions.question: The highest dam in India is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tehri Dam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Tehri Dam** is the **highest dam in India** and ranks among the top ten tallest dams globally, with a height of **260.5 meters** (855 feet).
 
• It is situated on the **Bhagirathi River**, the principal headstream of the **Ganges**, in the **Tehri Garhwal** district of **Uttarakhand**.
 
• The dam is a multi-purpose **rock and earth-fill embankment dam** that facilitates irrigation, municipal water supply, and the generation of **1,000 MW** of **hydroelectricity**.
 
• The project was commissioned in **2006** and includes a reservoir, known as **Tehri Lake**, which covers an area of approximately **52 square kilometers**.
 
• The structural design was intended to withstand high-intensity **seismic activity**, as it is located in the high-risk **Seismic Zone V** of the Himalayan region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bhakra Nangal Dam**:

 
 
• Located on the **Satluj River** in **Himachal Pradesh**, it is the **highest gravity dam** in India, standing at **225.55 meters**.
 
• Its massive reservoir is known as the **Gobind Sagar Lake**, named after the tenth Sikh Guru.
 
 
 
• **Hirakud Dam**:
 
 
• Built across the **Mahanadi River** in **Odisha**, it is distinguished as the **longest dam in the world**, with a total length of **ckilometers**.
 
• It was one of the first major multi-purpose river valley projects started after India’s independence.
 
 
 
• **Sardar Sarovar Dam**:
 
 
• A **concrete gravity dam** built on the **Narmada River** in **Gujarat**, it is the largest structure of the **Narmada Valley Project**.
 
• It has a height of **138.68 meters** and is one of the largest water resources projects in the world, covering four states.

questions.question: Who among the following was a noted historian of the Sultanate period?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ziauddin Barani**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ziauddin Barani** (1285−1358 AD) was a prominent Muslim political thinker and chronicler who lived during the **Delhi Sultanate** period, specifically serving in the court of **Muhammad bin Tughlaq** for seventeen years.
 
• His magnum opus, **Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi**, is regarded as one of the most significant historical works of medieval India, providing a chronological account of the **Delhi Sultanate** from the accession of **Ghiyasuddin Balban** in 1266 to the first six years of **Firoz Shah Tughlaq**'s reign in 1357.
 
• Barani provided a highly detailed record of the administrative, agrarian, and economic reforms introduced by **Alauddin Khalji**, including his famous **Market Control Policy** and price stabilization measures.
 
• He also authored the **Fatwa-i-Jahandari**, which is a treatise on political philosophy and statecraft, outlining the ideal conduct for a Muslim ruler and the legal framework of the **Sultanate**.
 
• His historiography is noted for its focus on the 'truth' of history and its didactic purpose, aimed at providing moral lessons and guidance to future kings and bureaucrats.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Abul Fazl**:

 
 
• He was the court historian and **Grand Vizier** of the **Mughal Emperor Akbar**.
 
• He is famous for writing the **Akbarnama** and the **Ain-i-Akbari**, which are monumental sources for 16th-century **Mughal** history.
 
 
 
• **Al-Biruni**:
 
 
• A Persian polymath who accompanied **Mahmud of Ghazni** to India in the early 11th century.
 
• He wrote **Kitab-ul-Hind** (Tarik-al-Hind), an encyclopedic work on Indian culture, science, and religion, predating the establishment of the **Delhi Sultanate**.
 
 
 
• **Amir Khusrau**:
 
 
• Known as the **Tut-i-Hind** (Parrot of India), he was a prolific poet, musician, and scholar associated with the courts of seven different Sultans.
 
• Though he documented historical events in works like **Tughlaq Nama** and **Khaza'in ul-Futuh**, he is primarily celebrated as a pioneer of **Sufi music** and **Khariboli** literature.

questions.question: What is the main objective of the Ayush Oushadhi Gunvatta evam Uttpadan Samvardhan Yojana launched in 2025?

options.text: To regulate food safety in India
To create AYUSH hospitals only in urban areas

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To support Ayush Pharmacies**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ayush Oushadhi Gunvatta evam Uttpadan Samvardhan Yojana (AOGUSY)** is a comprehensive **Central Sector Scheme** designed to enhance the quality and production of **Ayurveda, Siddha, Unani, and Homoeopathy (ASU&H)** drugs.
 
• A primary objective of the scheme is to provide financial and technical assistance for the **strengthening and upgradation** of **Ayush Pharmacies** and **Drug Testing Laboratories** across India.
 
• The scheme aims to facilitate **Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP)** compliance among manufacturers to ensure the production of high-quality traditional medicines that meet global standards.
 
• It serves as an umbrella initiative that integrates various components to improve the **regulatory framework** and surveillance of **Ayush medicines** at both Central and State levels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ministry of Ayush**:

 
 
• The scheme is implemented under the aegis of the **Ministry of Ayush** to bolster the domestic traditional medicine industry.
 
• It supports the **Atmanirbhar Bharat** initiative by reducing dependency on imported raw materials and enhancing export potential.
 
 
 
• **Target Beneficiaries**:
 
 
• Includes **State Government pharmacies** and **Drug Testing Labs** (DTLs) for infrastructure development.
 
• Focuses on **Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs)** within the Ayush sector to help them achieve **WHO-GMP** certification.
 
 
 
• **Regulatory Oversight**:
 
 
• The scheme supports the **Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy (PCIM&H)** in developing standardized protocols.
 
• It funds the **Quality Control of ASU&H drugs** to prevent the sale of sub-standard or adulterated medicines in the market.

questions.question: Which scheme was launched in Maharashtra in September 2024 to support early-stage women-led startups?

options.text: Punyashlok Ahilyadevi Holkar Women Startup Scheme

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Punyashlok Ahilyadevi Holkar Women Startup Scheme**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Punyashlok Ahilyadevi Holkar Women Startup Scheme** was officially launched in **September 2024** by the **Government of Maharashtra** to provide financial assistance and technical support specifically to **women-led startups** in their early stages.
 
• Under this scheme, eligible startups can receive financial aid ranging from **1 lakh to 25 lakh**, which is intended to cover initial capital requirements, prototype development, and market entry costs.
 
• To qualify for the benefits, a startup must be registered in **Maharashtra**, and women entrepreneurs must hold at least **51% shareholding** or ownership in the entity for at least **one year**.
 
• The initiative is managed by the **Maharashtra State Innovation Society (MSInS)** under the **Department of Skill Development, Employment, Entrepreneurship and Innovation**, aiming to bridge the gender gap in the state's entrepreneurial ecosystem.
 
• The scheme focuses on promoting **self-reliance (Atmanirbharta)** among women and boosting the state's contribution to India's **startup economy** by nurturing high-potential innovative ideas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Punyashlok Ahilyadevi Holkar**:

 
 
• She was the legendary **Maratha Queen** of the **Malwa kingdom**, renowned for her justice, administrative excellence, and significant role in building temples and dharamshalas across India.
 
 
 
• **Acharya Chanakya Skill Development Scheme**:
 
 
• Launched alongside the women startup scheme in **September 2024**, this initiative aims to establish **Skill Development Centers** in renowned colleges across Maharashtra to train over **1,50,000 youths** annually.
 
 
 
• **Maharashtra Innovation Landscape**:
 
 
• Maharashtra has consistently been recognized as a **Top Performer** in the **States' Startup Ranking** conducted by the **Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT)**.
 
• The state is home to one of the largest clusters of **Unicorns** and **Registered Startups** in the country, supported by the **Maharashtra State Innovative Startup Policy**.

questions.question:
Which of the following national park is located in Gujarat?

I. Gir National Park

II. Bandipur National Park
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gir National Park and Wildlife Sanctuary**, also known as **Sasan Gir**, is located in the **Junagadh**, **Gir Somnath**, and **Amreli** districts of **Gujarat**. Established in **1965**, it is the only natural habitat in the world for the **Asiatic Lion** (*Panthera leo leo*). The park is a part of the **Kathiawar-Gir dry deciduous forests** ecoregion and plays a vital role in the conservation of various species, including the **Indian Leopard** and **Chital**. ***Hence, statement I is correct.***
 
• **Bandipur National Park** is situated in the **Chamarajanagar** district of **Karnataka**. It was established as a **Tiger Reserve** under **Project Tiger** in **1974**. It forms a significant part of the **Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve**, bordering the **Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuary** in **Kerala** and the **Mudumalai National Park** in **Tamil Nadu**. ***Hence, statement II is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gujarat** hosts several other important protected areas:

 
 
• **Marine National Park**: Located in the **Gulf of Kutch**, it was **India** first marine park, established in **1982** to protect **coral reefs**, **sea turtles**, and **dugongs**.
 
• **Blackbuck National Park**: Situated in **Velavadar**, it is dedicated to the conservation of the **Indian Antelope** (Blackbuck).
 
• **Vansda National Park**: Located in the **Navsari** district, it represents the thick woodlands of the **Dangs** and the **Western Ghats**.
 
• **Wild Ass Sanctuary**: Located in the **Little Rann of Kutch**, it is the only home to the **Indian Wild Ass** (Khur).

questions.question: What is the meaning of Geoid?

options.text: It means a sun like massive size.
It means a planet without moon.
It means an earth like shape.
It means a massive size black hole.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**an earth like shape**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **Geoid** is derived from the Greek words **Geo** (meaning Earth) and **Eidos** (meaning form or shape), which literally translates to **Earth-shaped**.
 
• Geometrically, the **Earth** is not a perfect sphere; it is slightly flattened at the **North Pole** and **South Pole** while exhibiting a distinct bulge at the **Equator**.
 
• Scientific observations confirm that the **Geoid** represents the **Equipotential Surface** of the Earth's **Gravity Field**, which corresponds to the **Mean Sea Level** if the oceans were at rest and extended through the continents.
 
• The **Geoid** model is essential because it accounts for the uneven distribution of **Mass** within the Earth, causing local variations in **Gravitational Pull** that a simple ellipsoid cannot represent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Structural Dimensions:
 
 
• The **Equatorial Diameter** of the Earth is approximately **12,756 km**, whereas the **Polar Diameter** is about **12,714 km**.
 
• This difference of **42 km** classifies the Earth as an **Oblate Spheroid**, a shape directly resulting from the **Centrifugal Force** generated by the planet's **Rotation**.
 
 
 
• Practical Applications:
 
 
• **Geodesy** is the primary scientific discipline that utilizes the **Geoid** model for high-precision **Mapping** and surveying.
 
• Modern **Global Positioning Systems (GPS)** use geoid calculations to determine accurate **Orthometric Heights** (elevation above sea level) rather than just simple geometric height.
 
• Satellite missions like **GOCE** (Gravity Field and Steady-State Ocean Circulation Explorer) are dedicated to measuring the **Geoid** with extreme accuracy to study **Ocean Circulation** and **Climate Change**.

questions.question: _______ is a point on the orbit where vertical distance of the satellite from the earth's surface is smallest.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Perigee**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **orbital mechanics**, most satellites do not follow a perfectly circular path but instead move in an **elliptical orbit** around the **Earth**, as described by **Kepler's First Law**.
 
• The **Perigee** is defined as the specific point in this elliptical orbit where the satellite is at its **minimum distance** (closest proximity) to the **Earth's center** and surface.
 
• At the perigee, the satellite experiences the strongest **gravitational pull**, which results in it reaching its **maximum orbital velocity** to maintain its path.
 
• The term is derived from the **Greek** words **peri**, meaning near, and **gee**, meaning Earth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Apogee**:

 
 
• This refers to the point in the orbit where the satellite is at its **maximum distance** from the Earth.
 
• Due to the increased distance and weaker **gravitational influence**, the satellite moves at its **lowest orbital speed** at this point.
 
 
 
• **Inclination**:
 
 
• It represents the **angular distance** between the **orbital plane** of the satellite and the **equatorial plane** of the Earth.
 
• An inclination of **90 degrees** signifies a **polar orbit**, while **0 degrees** signifies an **equatorial orbit**.
 
 
 
• **Lagrange Point**:
 
 
• These are five specific positions (**L1 to L5**) in an orbital configuration where the **gravitational forces** of two large bodies (like the **Sun and Earth**) and the **centrifugal force** felt by a smaller object are in balance.
 
• They are often used for **space telescopes**, such as the **James Webb Space Telescope (JWST)**, because they allow a spacecraft to stay in a fixed position with **minimal fuel consumption**.

questions.question: How many modules will the Bharatiya Antariksh Station consist of?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bharatiya Antariksh Station (BAS)** is the planned modular space station to be constructed by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)**, representing India's first independent space station project.
 
• The **Union Cabinet of India** officially approved the project in **September 2024**, expanding the scope of the **Gaganyaan** program to include the development of the station's first module.
 
• The complete architecture of the **Bharatiya Antariksh Station** is designed to consist of **5** distinct modules, which will be launched and assembled in orbit sequentially.
 
• The phased deployment strategy targets the launch of the first module, **BAS-1**, by **2028**, with the full **5-module** assembly expected to be completed and operational by **2035**.
 
• This facility is intended to support **microgravity research** and will allow a crew of **3 to 4 astronauts** to stay in space for durations ranging from **15 to 20 days**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Technical and Strategic Specifications:**

 
 
• The total mass of the **BAS** upon completion will be approximately **52 tonnes**, and it will be positioned in a **Low Earth Orbit (LEO)** at an altitude of approximately **400 kilometers**.
 
• The **LVM3 (Launch Vehicle Mark 3)**, India's most powerful launch vehicle, will be utilized to ferry the modules into space.
 
• The station is a cornerstone of the **Amrit Kaal** vision for **2047**, which includes landing an Indian on the **Moon by 2040** and building a **lunar base by 2047**.
 
• The **5** modules are anticipated to include a core module, a science/research laboratory, a crew habitation module, a cargo module, and a dedicated docking port for **Gaganyaan** spacecraft and other visiting vessels.

questions.question: The United Nations Security Council has how many non-permanent members?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **United Nations Security Council (UNSC)** is composed of a total of **15 members**, which includes **5 permanent members** and **10 non-permanent members**.
 
• The **10 non-permanent members** are elected by the **United Nations General Assembly** for a **two-year term**.
 
• Each year, the General Assembly elects **five non-permanent members** to ensure a staggered transition; retiring members are not eligible for **immediate re-election**.
 
• The distribution of these **10 seats** is based on **equitable geographical representation**: **5 seats** for **African and Asian States**, **1 seat** for **Eastern European States**, **2 seats** for **Latin American and Caribbean States**, and **2 seats** for **Western European and Other States**.
 
• The primary mandate of the **UNSC** is to maintain **international peace and security** as defined in the **UN Charter**.
 
• To be elected, a candidate country must receive at least a **two-thirds majority** of the votes from the **General Assembly**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Permanent Members (P5)**:

 
 
• The **5 permanent members** are **China**, **France**, the **Russian Federation**, the **United Kingdom**, and the **United States**.
 
• These nations possess **veto power**, meaning any one of them can block a **substantive resolution** regardless of the level of international support.
 
 
 
• **Council Composition History**:
 
 
• The council originally consisted of **11 members** (5 permanent and 6 non-permanent).
 
• An amendment to **Article 23** of the **UN Charter** was adopted in **1963** and came into effect in **1965**, increasing the non-permanent membership from **6 to 10**.
 
 
 
• **Voting Procedures**:
 
 
• Each member of the Security Council has **one vote**.
 
• Decisions on **procedural matters** require an affirmative vote of at least **9 members**.

questions.question: India joined the Badminton World Federation in ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1936**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India became an official member of the **International Badminton Federation (IBF)**, which is now known as the **Badminton World Federation (BWF)**, in the year **1936**.
 
• The **Badminton Association of India (BAI)** was established in **1934** to manage and promote the sport within the country, coinciding with the global formation of the IBF.
 
• Joining the federation in **1936** allowed Indian athletes to compete in prestigious international tournaments and facilitated the growth of organized badminton competitions across the nation.
 
• The federation initially started with nine founding members, and India was one of the early nations to affiliate from the Asian continent, helping to internationalize the sport during its foundational years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Badminton World Federation (BWF)**:

 
 
• It was founded on **July 5, 1934**, and serves as the world governing body for the sport of badminton recognized by the **International Olympic Committee (IOC)**.
 
• The headquarters of the BWF is currently located in **Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia**.
 
• The organization was renamed from the International Badminton Federation to the **Badminton World Federation** in **September 2006**.
 
 
 
• **History and Milestones in India**:
 
 
• The modern game of badminton is widely believed to have originated in **Pune**, India, during the **1860s**, where it was locally referred to as **Poona**.
 
• The **first national championship** in India was held in **1934**, the same year the national association was formed.
 
• Legendary player **Prakash Padukone** created history by becoming the first Indian to win the **All England Open Badminton Championships** in **1980**.
 
• The **Thomas Cup** victory in **2022** remains one of India's greatest achievements in team badminton under the BWF umbrella.

questions.question: As of 31st July 2025, the men's 200-metre sprint world record is ____ seconds.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**19.19**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The world record for the men's **200-metre sprint** is **19.19 seconds**, a mark that has stood for over a decade.
 
• This extraordinary feat was achieved by **Usain Bolt** of **Jamaica**, widely regarded as the fastest human in recorded history.
 
• The record was set on **August 20, 2009**, during the **12th IAAF World Championships in Athletics** held in **Berlin, Germany**.
 
• Bolt surpassed his own previous world record of **19.30 seconds**, which he had established exactly one year prior at the **2008 Beijing Olympics**.
 
• The performance in Berlin was particularly impressive as it was achieved with a **headwind** of **-0.3 m/s**, demonstrating Bolt's raw power and speed endurance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Usain Bolt's Legacy:**

 
 
• Bolt is the only sprinter to win **Olympic 100 m and 200 m titles** at three consecutive **Olympic Games** (2008, 2012, and 2016).
 
• At the same **2009 Berlin World Championships**, he also set the current world record for the **100-metre sprint** with a time of **9.58 seconds**.
 
• He retired from professional athletics in **2017** with a total of **11 World Championship gold medals** and **8 Olympic gold medals**.
 
 
 
• **Statistical Context of the 200m:**
 
 
• The second-fastest time in history is **19.26 seconds**, recorded by fellow Jamaican **Yohan Blake** in 2011.
 
• American sprinter **Noah Lyles** holds the third-fastest time and the **American record** at **19.31 seconds**, achieved in 2022.
 
• Before the Bolt era, the record was held by **Michael Johnson**, who ran **19.32 seconds** at the **1996 Atlanta Olympics**, a record that many experts believed would stand for decades.

questions.question: What is the primary reason for filling electric bulbs with chemically inactive gases like nitrogen and argon?

options.text: To increase the brightness of the light
To prolong the life of the filament
To reduce the cost of production

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To prolong the life of the filament**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The filament in an electric bulb is primarily made of **Tungsten**, a metal known for its extremely high **melting point** (approximately **3422 degrees Celsius**) and high **electrical resistance**.
 
• When electricity flows through the filament, it heats up and emits light through the process of **incandescence**; however, at such high temperatures, tungsten is prone to **oxidation** if it comes into contact with **oxygen** from the air.
 
• To prevent the filament from burning out immediately, the air is removed from the bulb and replaced with **chemically inactive gases** like **Argon** or **Nitrogen**.
 
• The presence of these **inert gases** creates a pressurized environment that significantly retards the **sublimation** or evaporation of tungsten atoms from the hot filament.
 
• By suppressing the rate of **tungsten evaporation** and preventing chemical reactions, these gases maintain the thickness of the wire, effectively **prolonging the life of the filament**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Inert Gases**:

 
 
• **Argon**: A **noble gas** that is the most frequently used filler because it does not react with the filament even at white-heat temperatures.
 
• **Nitrogen**: Often mixed with argon to suppress **arcing** (electrical discharge) between the lead-in wires, which can occur more easily in pure argon.
 
 
 
• **Scientific Principles**:
 
 
• **Joule Heating**: The production of heat in a conductor due to the passage of an electric current, governed by the formula **H = I²Rt**.
 
• **Tungsten Properties**: Chosen for its high **tensile strength** and low **vapor pressure** at high temperatures, ensuring the bulb remains functional for hundreds of hours.

questions.question: Which of the following is a solid musical instrument, shaped like a pitcher made of baked clay, and is found in Kashmir?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Noot**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Noot** is a traditional **percussion instrument** extensively used in the **Kashmir Valley** for folk and classical music.
 
• It is an **earthenware pitcher** made of **baked clay**, featuring a spherical body and a narrow neck, similar to a water pot (Ghara) but with a more refined structure for acoustic resonance.
 
• Categorized as a **Ghan Vadya** (idiophone), the sound is produced by striking the mouth, neck, and sides of the pot using the fingers and palms.
 
• The **Noot** is an integral part of **Kashmiri folk music**, specifically providing the rhythmic accompaniment for **Sufiana Kalam** and wedding songs known as **Wanwun**.
 
• To enhance the tonal quality and strength, the **baked clay** is sometimes reinforced with **brass** or **iron filings** during the manufacturing process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kasale**

 
 
• It is a traditional **percussion instrument** from **Karnataka**.
 
• Consists of a pair of **bronze cymbals** that are rhythmically struck together, primarily used in the folk dance form known as **Kamsale**.
 
 
 
• **Esraj**
 
 
• A **stringed instrument** (chordophone) common in **West Bengal** and parts of North India.
 
• It is played with a **bow** and is frequently used in **Rabindra Sangeet** and Hindustani classical music performances.
 
 
 
• **Pepa**
 
 
• A traditional **wind instrument** (aerophone) originating from **Assam**.
 
• It is crafted from **buffalo horn** and bamboo, and it plays a vital role in the music of the **Bihu festival**.

questions.question: Which of the following is a use of coke?

options.text: As a fuel for residential cooling

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**In the manufacture of steel**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Coke** is a tough, black, and porous solid substance that is an almost pure form of **carbon**, typically containing **90% to 98%** carbon content.
 
• It is produced through the process of **destructive distillation**, where high-quality bituminous coal is heated to temperatures exceeding **1000°C** in the absence of oxygen to remove volatile matter.
 
• The primary industrial application of coke is in the **manufacture of steel** and the **extraction of metals** from their naturally occurring ores.
 
• In a **blast furnace**, coke serves as a vital **reducing agent** that reacts with the oxygen in iron ore (such as **Fe₂O₃**) to produce molten iron and carbon dioxide.
 
• Besides its chemical role, coke acts as a high-efficiency **fuel** providing the extreme thermal energy required for melting metal ores during **smelting**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Physical Properties of Coke**:

 
 
• Coke is preferred over raw coal in **metallurgy** because it burns with very little smoke and has a higher **calorific value**.
 
• Its **porous structure** allows for the efficient flow of gases within industrial furnaces, facilitating uniform heating and chemical reactions.
 
 
 
• **Other Coal By-products**:
 
 
• **Coal Tar**: A thick, dark liquid obtained during coke production, used in the manufacture of **synthetic dyes**, **drugs**, **explosives**, **perfumes**, and **naphthalene balls**.
 
• **Coal Gas**: A flammable gaseous mixture of hydrogen, methane, and carbon monoxide used as an **industrial fuel** for heating.
